posts.author: Jem
posts.content_md:
Hi All

My new C315m laser arrived yesterday. I haven't had a chance to fire it up yet and don't expect to be able to do so for a couple of weeks or so. The laser has both the Digital and Analogue Coherent controllers with it, but unfortunately it doesn't have the autostart adapter.

Firstly, I wondered if anyone has ever written any PC software to control the laser via a RS-232 port linked to the digital controller. If so are there any hints and tips for using either Visual Basic or VB.net to acheive this. Even better is there anyone out there who has already done this and would care to share their program with me?

Alternatively, I would really like to get hold of an external control module. Something that gives easy user control and feedback on the state of the laser. I know Marconi used to make these and just wondered if anyone had one kicking around that they don't use anymore 

Oh, I don't expect it for nothing, cash is waiting 

I can't wait to start making some holograms with this laser. I've been in touch with Uli at Colourholographic and he's sending me some plates. Hopefully by the time I get back from a (very inconveniently timed) conference towards the end of June i'll have more time available - very frustrating.

Thanks folks

Jem

posts.author: Jem

Hi DJ

Thanks for the info 

I've pretty much read all of Sam's pages in relation to the C315m from top to bottom - WOW! there's some great information in there.

As previously mentioned i've been talking to Marconi about building me a user interface to link to the analogue controller. I've now heard back from him and he's agreed to build me one if I want to go down that road.

I'm off to a conference for a few days tomorrow, so the time to play about before I go is limited. But i'll provide an update on my return when i've had the time to play.

Cheers

Jem

posts.author: Jem
posts.content_md:
I've just had time for a quick 'Play' before I leave tomorrow.

I connected the power supply to the lasers analogue controller, connected the digital controller to my laptop using a null modem cable, started hyperterminal and adjusted the comms protocols according to the Coherent manual.

I switched everything on, typed the word 'On' into hyperterminal and hit the 'Enter' key....

WooHooo 

I've got a green beam 8) 

After a couple of minutes wait whilst it went through it's ramping procedure it settled out at a nice setpoint of 99.5mw. I have to say that the digital controller is VERY easy to use. I'm now inspired to write some software that will provide both control and feedback.

Can't wait to start making holograms 

Cheers

Jem

I have a heatsink mounted to the head and another one mounted to the analog controller. I added the controller heatsink after a few weeks because it was getting hot to the touch and I decided that it would not the best thing. Both were choosen to disipate the heat in a passive mode.

It is for TECs but the heatsink stuff works for anything.
